newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BOURSE TO MEDIATE BETWEEN PAINTMAKERS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BOURSE TO MEDIATE BETWEEN PAINTMAKERS.

text.p: A Warsaw bourse official agreed on Thursday to mediate between shareholders of Polifarb Cieszyn and Polifarb Wroclaw and help settle a row over the the paintmakers' merger plan.

Bourse chairman Leszek Juchniewicz told a news conference he was asked by the management boards of both firms, concerned that a conflict between their shareholders over how much they should get in the new firm could derail the whole merger plan.

"Today I have received the joint request of Polifarb Cieszyn and Polifarb Wroclaw to undertake the task of solving the conflicts and confusion which have arisen in the process of merging the two firms," Juchniewicz said.
"I decided to accept this request in order to help seek constructive solutions," he added.

Originally the managements of the merging firms agreed that shareholders were to get 50-50 in the merged company, but Polifarb Cieszyn's shareholders decided later that they should get 53.5 percent, increasing a pre-merger bonus issue for Cieszyn shareholders to 6.375 from 2.98 million shares.

But last week Polifarb Wroclaw said that the Treasury Ministry, which has 16 percent of Wroclaw shares, requested an extraordinary meeting and a new bonus issue of up to 10 million shares to shift control of the planned new company in favour of Wroclaw shareholders.
Cieszyn currently has 19,125,000 shares, 2,978,820 fewer than Wroclaw, and a bonus issue of that number of shares under the original 50-50 plan had been designed to make up for the difference.
